chats.answer:
For a dash cam with side cameras, I'd prioritize a true 4-channel system that records the front, rear, left, and right sides of your car.

The important distinction is that many dash cams advertised as 3-channel record the front, rear, and interior—not the exterior sides. If you're concerned about sideswipes, door dings, parking-lot damage, or hit-and-runs, exterior side coverage is much more useful.

My top choices are systems from Vantrue, Thinkware, and BlackVue, depending on whether you want maximum coverage, parking protection, or a discreet installation.

Best dash cams with left and right side coverage

1. Rexing R4 — Best overall for side coverage

Front + rear + left + right • 1080p on all four channels

$259.99

Adjustable side-facing lenses, GPS and Wi-Fi. Good for recording sideswipes without mounting cameras outside the car.

View at Rexing

2. Thinkware ARC800 + exterior side cameras — Best premium setup

4K front • Dedicated exterior left/right cameras • Expandable system

$279.99 base dash cam only

Add the compatible multiplexer and two waterproof 1080p side cameras. Better physical positioning for parking-lot damage, but requires more installation.

View base camera

3. REDTIGER 4-Channel 360° — Best budget option

Four adjustable lenses • 2.5K front/rear • 1080p side views

$209.99

Attractive specifications for the price, although I have less confidence in its long-term reliability than the more established alternatives.

View at Best Buy

Thinkware confirms that its multiplexer supports dedicated exterior side cameras and compatible multi-channel systems.

One model I'd avoid for your specific requirement is the Vantrue N5S. Although it's a well-reviewed four-channel dash cam, two of its cameras point into the cabin rather than directly outward at the left and right sides.

chats.answer:
If you're looking for the best dash cam with side cameras, I'd prioritize a system that records the front, rear, left, and right sides of your car.

Most dash cams advertised as "3-channel" only record the front, rear, and interior. They don't necessarily capture cars approaching from either side.

There are three main options:

True 4-side coverage: Best for parking damage, sideswipes, and hit-and-runs.

Front + rear + interior: Best for rideshare drivers, but limited exterior side coverage.

Front + rear + left/right side cameras: Best overall protection, though installation is more complicated.

Best dash cams with side coverage (2026)

1. G980H 3K 4-Camera 360° Dash Cam with GPS

Best overall pick
$229.00

3K front, 1080p rear and adjustable left/right cameras. Good balance of resolution and coverage.

2. Rexing - R4 4 Channel Dash Cam W/ All Around 1080p Resolutio…

$219.99

Four 1080p views, with side lenses that can be aimed through the side windows. Established option for exterior coverage.

3. F17 Plus 4-Channel 2.7K Dash Cam with Sony STARVIS 2 & Wi‑Fi

$199.99

Four-channel recording with Sony STARVIS 2 technology. Worth considering for low-light recording, although side-window performance should be verified.

4. Rexing C4 4-Channel Dash Cam with All-Around 1080p, Wi-Fi Ap…

$199.99

Budget-friendly four-channel option with adjustable side lenses and IR night vision.

These models use cameras positioned inside the vehicle, so reflections, window tint, and camera placement can limit exterior visibility. None guarantees complete coverage of the doors or blind spots.

My pick: The Botslab G980H for its 3K front recording and adjustable side views. The Rexing R4 is a good alternative if you prefer its straightforward four-camera layout.

One important question: Do you want the side cameras to record outside the car, especially while parked, or do you mainly want side coverage while driving?

That distinction changes which system I'd recommend.
